title: Hardcoded secret committed in application.properties (WrongSecrets)

ticket.title: Plaintext secret committed in src/main/resources/application.properties
ticket.problem_statement: A plaintext secret is committed directly into src/main/resources/application.properties (a password= property). Anyone with repository access can read it, and it is bound into the application at startup. The committed value must be removed and supplied at runtime via an environment variable / secret store instead, keeping the property binding but not the literal value.
acceptance_criteria: The plaintext secret is no longer present in application.properties
The value is provided at runtime via environment/secret store

pass_criteria: Plan targets the committed secret property in application.properties
Fix removes the literal value and sources it from the environment / secret store
The plaintext secret string no longer appears in the file

title: Plaintext-equivalent secret committed in a Kubernetes Secret manifest (WrongSecrets)

ticket.title: Kubernetes Secret manifest commits a base64 (not encrypted) secret value
ticket.problem_statement: A Kubernetes Secret manifest (k8s/secrets-secret.yml) commits a secret value as base64 in the repository. Base64 is encoding, not encryption, so the secret is effectively in plaintext in version control and is exposed to the workload via env. The committed value must be removed/rotated and the secret sourced securely (external secret store / sealed secret), with the workload consuming it via a mounted secret rather than a committed manifest value.
acceptance_criteria: The committed base64 secret value is removed/rotated from the manifest
The secret is sourced from a secure store rather than committed in VCS

pass_criteria: Plan targets the committed Secret value in k8s/secrets-secret.yml
Fix removes/rotates the committed value and sources it securely
The committed base64 secret no longer appears in the manifest
